```{r, include = FALSE}
# chunks run on the example file shipped with the package
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  eval = TRUE)

# ggplot2 is suggested only, so its chunks are skipped when it is absent
has_ggplot2 <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)

```



This vignette shows how to extract raw nanopore signals from POD5 files with **pod5R**, and how to plot them with base R graphics or ggplot2. Two workflows are covered: direct extraction by read identifier, and extraction preceded by reading the per-read metadata. We recommend the second one whenever reads have to be selected by their properties, or when the signal should be shown on a time axis. Plotting of many reads is covered in `vignette("batch_plotting")`.

All examples use a small direct RNA sequencing (DRS) file shipped with the package. The same calls work for any POD5 file.

> **Note:** pod5R provides read-only access. It does not segment the signal, detect poly(A) tails, or perform basecalling.


## Example data

The example file is a real toy DRS dataset provided with the package. File-level information can be retrieved with `read_pod5_info()`:


```{r example-data}
pod5_file <- system.file("extdata", "drs-filtered.pod5",
                         package = "pod5R", mustWork = TRUE)

pod5R::read_pod5_info(pod5_file)
```



To work with your own data, assign the path to your POD5 file to `pod5_file` instead. All the following calls in this vignette then work unchanged:

```{r user-file, eval = FALSE}
# path to your own POD5 file
pod5_file <- "/path/to/user/provided/file.pod5"

pod5R::read_pod5_info(pod5_file)
```



## Extraction without reading metadata first


### Read identifiers


`read_pod5_ids()` returns read identifiers (UUIDs) in file order. No signal data are decompressed at this stage.

```{r read-ids}

read_ids <- pod5R::read_pod5_ids(pod5_file)

length(read_ids)
head(read_ids, 3)
```


### Raw signal

`extract_pod5_signal()` returns a list of signal vectors named by read UUID, in the requested order. By default, signals are returned raw, as integer ADC counts.

```{r raw-signal}

raw_list <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(pod5_file, read_ids = read_ids[1])

str(raw_list)
```

### Calibrated signal

With `calibrated = TRUE`, signals are returned as numeric vectors in picoamperes (pA). Calibration uses the per-read values stored in the file and is computed using formula `(raw_signal + calibration_offset) * calibration_scale`.

```{r calibrated-signal}

pa_list <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(pod5_file,
                                      read_ids = read_ids[1],
                                      calibrated = TRUE)

str(pa_list)
```

### Signal intervals

A part of the signal can be requested with `start_sample` and `end_sample`. Both coordinates are one-based and inclusive. Only compressed chunks overlapping the interval are decoded, so the extraction of short windows stays fast even for long reads. Bounds beyond the end of the read are clipped.


In this example below, the interval is stored in two variables, `window_start` and `window_end`. They are reused in the [Plotting](#plotting) section, so the extraction
and the plot always correspond to the same read samples.

```{r signal-interval}
# window used here and in the plotting section below
window_start <- 2600
window_end <- 4500

window_list <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(pod5_file,
                                          read_ids = read_ids[1],
                                          calibrated = TRUE,
                                          start_sample = window_start,
                                          end_sample = window_end)

length(window_list[[1]])
```



## Extraction with reading metadata first

### Read metadata

`read_pod5()` returns one row of metadata per read. Unless `signal = TRUE` is set, the signal data are not decompressed, so the whole file can be scanned cheaply.

Opening a reader inspects every read batch of the file. When several calls are made on the same file, the reader should be opened only once with `open_pod5()`, reusing it, and closing it with `close_pod5()`.

```{r read-metadata}

reader <- pod5R::open_pod5(pod5_file)

reads <- pod5R::read_pod5(reader)

colnames(reads)
head(reads[, c("read_id", "num_samples", "sample_rate", "end_reason")], 3)

```



### Selecting reads

Reads can be selected with ordinary R subsetting. In the example below, the read closest to the median signal length is chosen as a representative.

```{r select-read}

# read closest to the median signal length
selected <- reads[which.min(abs(reads$num_samples - stats::median(reads$num_samples))), ]

selected[, c("read_id", "num_samples", "sample_rate")]

```



### Metadata and signal in one call

With `signal = TRUE`, `read_pod5()` returns a named list with `reads` (metadata in the requested order) and `signal` (vectors named by UUID). By this, the
calibration values and the sample rate are kept next to the signal.

```{r metadata-signal}

out <- pod5R::read_pod5(reader,
                        read_ids = selected$read_id,
                        signal = TRUE)

names(out)

str(out[['signal']])

pod5R::close_pod5(reader)
```



Calibration can be reproduced from the raw signal and the metadata. The result is consistent to the output of `calibrated = TRUE`:


```{r manual-calibration}

raw_signal <- out[['signal']][[1]]
pa_signal <- (raw_signal + out[['reads']]$calibration_offset) * out[['reads']]$calibration_scale

# assertion
all.equal(pa_signal,
          pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(pod5_file,
                                     read_ids = selected$read_id,
                                     calibrated = TRUE)[[1]])

```


## Plotting

The signal is plotted in acquisition order. Without metadata, the x axis shows the sample position. With metadata, positions are converted to time using the read `sample_rate`. The first sample placed at 0 s.

```{r plot-data}

signal_df <- data.frame(
  position = seq_along(raw_signal),
  # rescale time to seconds
  time = (seq_along(raw_signal) - 1) / out[['reads']]$sample_rate,
  raw = raw_signal,
  pa = pa_signal)

head(signal_df, 3)

```


Plotting every sample of very long reads may be slow and place heavy load on memory. In such scenarios, extracting only interval with `start_sample` and `end_sample` is recommended.


### Base R 

Raw signal on the sample axis (no metadata required):


```{r base-raw, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.5}

graphics::plot(signal_df$position, signal_df$raw,
               type = "l",
               col = "#3a414d",
               xlab = "position [samples]",
               ylab = "signal [ADC counts]",
               main = "Raw signal")
```


Calibrated signal on the time axis (samples converted to seconds):

```{r base-calibrated, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.5}

graphics::plot(signal_df$time, signal_df$pa,
               type = "l",
               col = "#3a414d",
               xlab = "time [s]",
               ylab = "signal [pA]",
               main = "Calibrated signal")
```



### ggplot2

The examples below require ggplot2 to be installed; otherwise, their chunks are skipped.


```{r ggplot-calibrated, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.5}

g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(signal_df, ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = pa))
g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")
g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Calibrated signal",
                        x = "time [s]",
                        y = "signal [pA]")

plot_signal <- g.base + g.line + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()

print(plot_signal)
```



Raw and calibrated signals can be compared in two panels. Since calibration only shifts and scales the signal, both panels have the same shape:

```{r ggplot-comparison, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}

scale_levels <- c("raw [ADC counts]", "calibrated [pA]")

comparison_df <- data.frame(
  position = rep(signal_df$position, 2),
  signal = c(signal_df$raw, signal_df$pa),
  scale = factor(rep(scale_levels, each = nrow(signal_df)), levels = scale_levels))

g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(comparison_df, ggplot2::aes(x = position, y = signal))
g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")
g.facet <- ggplot2::facet_wrap(~scale, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y")
g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Raw and calibrated signal",
                        x = "position [samples]",
                        y = NULL)

plot_comparison <- g.base + g.line + g.facet + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()
print(plot_comparison)

```

### Signal interval

A signal interval is plotted the same way. Positions are offset by `start_sample`, so that the x axis keeps the whole-read coordinates.

In the example below, the interval delimited by `window_start` and `window_end` is extracted from the selected read (the same previous one, i.e. the read already shown in the plots above), The read identifier is displayed in the subtitle of both plots.


```{r ggplot-interval, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.5}

window_signal <- pod5R::extract_pod5_signal(pod5_file,
                                            read_ids = selected$read_id,
                                            calibrated = TRUE,
                                            start_sample = window_start,
                                            end_sample = window_end)[[1]]

# assertion - whether the interval equals the same samples of the whole read
# should return TRUE
identical(window_signal, signal_df$pa[window_start:window_end])

# positions keep the coordinates of the whole read
window_df <- data.frame(
  position = window_start + seq_along(window_signal) - 1,
  pa = window_signal
)
```


The whole signal, with the extracted interval shaded:


```{r ggplot-whole-shaded, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.5}
g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(signal_df, ggplot2::aes(x = position, y = pa))
g.rect <- ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = window_start, xmax = window_end,
                            ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#449434", alpha = .15)
g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")
g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Whole calibrated signal",
                        subtitle = paste0(selected$read_id, ", interval ",
                                          window_start, "-", window_end),
                        x = "position [samples]",
                        y = "signal [pA]")

plot_full <- g.base + g.rect + g.line + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()
print(plot_full)

```

The interval alone. For the purpose of this example, the poly(A) tail was selected. Its shape matches the shaded part of the plot above:

```{r ggplot-interval, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.5}
g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(window_df, ggplot2::aes(x = position, y = pa))
g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")
g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Calibrated signal interval",
                        subtitle = selected$read_id,
                        x = "position [samples]",
                        y = "signal [pA]")

plot_window <- g.base + g.line + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()
print(plot_window)
```



To inspect another chunk of the read, `window_start` and `window_end` should be changed and the interval chunks are run again. Changing only the positions in
`window_df` would relabel the x axis without extracting different part of the signal




## Summary of functions used

| Function | Description | Decompresses signal |
|---|---|---|
| `read_pod5_info()` | File-level information | no |
| `read_pod5_ids()` | Read identifiers in file order | no |
| `read_pod5()` | Read metadata; signal with `signal = TRUE` | only with `signal = TRUE` |
| `extract_pod5_signal()` | Raw or calibrated signal vectors | yes |
| `open_pod5()` / `close_pod5()` | Open and close a reusable reader | no |
